chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever forgets to pray the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf until he leaves Mecca, he must make it up, or his guardian or a Muslim man may make it up for him." If he forgets the two rak'ahs until he has performed five circuits between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, he should cut off the Sa'i, come to the Maqam (of Ibrahim), pray the two rak'ahs, then return and complete the Sa'i. This was narrated.

key_terms.السَّعْي: The Sa'i, walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةُ: Safa and Marwah, the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer following the obligatory Tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The obligatory circumambulation of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer before or during Sa'i?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the sequence of Hajj rituals, emphasizing that the two rak'ahs of Tawaf are a confirmed Sunnah rather than a strict prerequisite for Sa'i. It highlights the scholarly principle of *qada* (making up) in ritual prayer, allowing for either personal fulfillment or vicarious performance by a representative, which underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) intended by the Shariah for pilgrims.
